races.name: Easter Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Celestra
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 271-day break with fitness concerns but uncontested lead suits her style perfectly

runners_data.name: Sierra Sue
runners_data.note: Expensive newcomer with strong breeding but completely unknown quantity making debut for in-form connections
runners_data.comment: Quite a speedy pedigree to start out over this trip but still needs a betting check
runners_data.spotlight: £42,000 Starman half-sister to winners Roman Spring (5f/6f including AW; RPR 76) and Only In Jakarta (7f AW; 76); dam unraced half-sister to 5f Listed winner Swiss Lake (dam of sprint Group 3 winners Swiss Spirit and Swiss Diva); arguably a bit of a surprise to see her start over an extended 1m given the speed in her pedigree but still worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who shaped well at Sandown and should appreciate the step up in trip from her debut efforts
runners_data.comment: Third on debut; beaten at 5-6 since but evidently well regarded and given another chance
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly who cost 260,000gns as a yearling; shaped well when third of seven in Sandown maiden (7f, soft) on debut, with subsequent Prix Marcel Boussac fourth Esna only narrowly ahead of her in second; on the back of that she went off at 4-5 for a Newbury novice (1m, soft) in October but faded into fifth (Lovers Leap sixth); evidently well regarded and given another chance to confirm that debut promise.

runners_data.name: Yorkies Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs a strong pace to aim at but showed ability when third on Redcar debut
runners_data.comment: Modest third on Redcar debut and well held at Bath next time
runners_data.spotlight: Finished well for third of five on 7f Redcar debut (good to soft) last October but form is nothing specials and she was well beaten at Bath later in the month.

runners_data.name: Lillie Margot
runners_data.note: Lightly raced type who ran well on debut at Haydock but disappointed when favorite next time out
runners_data.comment: Promise on first of two 1m starts last year; retains potential on return
runners_data.spotlight: Nice debut when chasing home a couple of useful sorts over 1m at Haydock (good) last September; only seventh when favourite at Leicester (1m again) the following month but she retains potential on her return.

runners_data.name: Lovers Leap
runners_data.note: Expensive yearling purchase who can race prominently but may struggle with the step up to this trip
runners_data.comment: Promise on AW debut but only sixth on soft turf next time; cheekpieces added on return
runners_data.spotlight: 450,000gns yearling; showed some promise with fourth of nine on 7f Wolverhampton debut in September; perhaps soft ground didn't suit when sixth (Thankfully fifth) of eight at Newbury (1m) later in the autumn; cheekpieces are reached for on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Wheres Veneker
runners_data.note: Recent Newcastle debut was poor and significant improvement needed on turf switch for this weak performer
runners_data.comment: 50-1 and finished down the field on 7f Newcastle debut five weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: 50-1 and finished down the field on 7f Newcastle debut five weeks ago; significant improvement needed now switching to turf.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Geisha
runners_data.note: Showed nothing on Wolverhampton debut and appears outclassed against these more experienced rivals
runners_data.comment: 25-1 and no short-term promise on 9.4f Wolverhampton debut last month
runners_data.spotlight: 25-1 and no short-term promise on 9.4f Wolverhampton debut last month.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from all-weather to turf with two recent Tapeta runs providing fitness foundation
runners_data.comment: Modest form in two AW outings this year
runners_data.spotlight: Two outings on Tapeta this year, beaten just under 10l when third over 8.6f at Wolverhampton latterly; improvement needed now switching to turf.

races.paceDynamic: Celestra will lead uncontested from the start, setting her own tempo without early pressure from this small field. Thankfully and Lovers Leap will track in second and third respectively, but neither appears keen to challenge early. The lack of pace pressure means Celestra can dictate fractions and save energy for the finish, while hold-up horses like Yorkies Dream and Aurelune will need the leaders to come back to them. This controlled tempo strongly favors front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without expending excessive energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Celestra Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Celestra maintains her lead without serious early pressure and dictates moderate fractions.
scenarios.body: She can use her class advantage to kick clear in the straight while saving energy from the uncontested lead. The patient tempo allows her to have enough left for a sustained finish that the hold-up horses cannot match.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Thankfully or Lovers Leap can sit close enough to Celestra and produce stronger late kicks.
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows prominent runners to conserve energy while staying in touch, then outstay the leader in the final furlong. Their superior finishing kicks prove decisive over the staying trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and allows back-markers to close significant ground.
scenarios.body: Yorkies Dream or Aurelune benefit from a crawling pace that neutralizes the front-runner's advantage. They produce sweeping late runs that catch the leaders who have gone too slowly early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Sierra Sue shows the ability her breeding suggests and can track the pace effectively.
scenarios.body: The expensive newcomer uses natural ability to overcome inexperience, sitting handy before striking late. Her half-sister connections to winners at similar trips provide the genetic foundation for immediate success.

watchPoints.text: Celestra's 271-day absence could see her fade badly in the final furlong if fitness is lacking after the long break
Sierra Sue's market movements will reveal connections' confidence in this expensive but unraced Starman half-sister
Thankfully's settling ability early will determine if she can produce her best finishing kick from an ideal position
The early fractions set by Celestra will dictate whether hold-up horses like Yorkies Dream have any realistic chance
Lovers Leap's ability to handle the step up to 1m4f remains untested given her shorter distance experience

races.name: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc') (Div I)

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.comment: Yard doesn't have many 2yos go in first time; best watched unless betting hints otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: February foal by Mohaather; 16,000euros foal; dam 6f-1m maiden in UAE (RPR 64), half-sister to US 1m Grade 3 winner Carressa, out of US 1m/8.5f stakes winner; stable doesn't have many 2yos go in first time; best watched unless the betting hints otherwise

runners_data.name: Donna Rumma
runners_data.comment: Market confidence significant for a stable quick to get among 2yo winners this year
runners_data.spotlight: This February foal cost £31,000 as a yearling and is the first foal of a 6f AW winner (RPR 89); stable quick to get among the juvenile winners this year and market confidence would look very significant.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.comment: One of three newcomers from the stable and the betting should provide more clues
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; 22,000gns half-sister to winners Song Of The Clyde (6f 2yo; RPR 96) and Flicka's Girl (5f/6f AW inc 2yo; 75); dam 5f AW 2yo winner (57); one of three newcomers for a yard which won this in 2019 (second time up) and sent out the useful Argentine Tango to finish second on debut last year.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.comment: Makes plenty of paper appeal for good stable
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; half-sister to 6f winner Diligently (including 2yo; RPR 91); dam was a 6f winner and is a half-sister to winners Audience (1m Group 1), Esquire (7f Group 3) and Dark Lady (6f 2yo Group 3); makes plenty of paper appeal and very interesting to see what the betting makes of her.

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.comment: Betting check needed for a stable which has tasted success in this race in recent years
runners_data.spotlight: This February foal is a half-sister to winners Grand Libya (French 6.5f-1m AW; RPR 87) and Cancan In The Rain (7f/1m including 2yo/AW; 84); dam French 1m1f winner, half-sister to winners Starboard (1m2f Group 3) and Predilection (Listed-placed 1m); market check needed for a stable which has tasted success in this race in recent years.

runners_data.name: Baila Morena
runners_data.comment: The youngest in the line-up and probably best watched
runners_data.spotlight: The youngest in the line-up as an April foal; 3,000gns half-sister to 5f winner Bobbi Rosa (RPR 88); dam unraced half-sister to winners Soldier's Call (5f 2yo Group 2); probably best watched.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.comment: Likely type for top yard which won this with one in the Nick Bradley silks last year
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 18,000euros half-sister to winners Dark Rosa (6f turf 2yo/8.6f AW; RPR 77) and Tiger Mylk (1m 2yo; 68); Karl Burke won this with one in the same colours last year; likely type

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.comment: Tasleet filly who is best watched on debut unless betting strongly suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: This daughter of Tasleet is a January foal and the first out of a mare who was placed over 1m2f on AW (RPR 76); others make greater paper appeal.

races.name: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc') (Div II)

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.comment: Handily drawn and hails from excellent stable so reasons to be positive
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £31,000 Acclamation filly and the second foal of a 5f winner (including 2yo; RPR 94); has a handy draw and hails from an excellent stable so there are reasons to be positive.

runners_data.name: Stripes Of Glory
runners_data.comment: Worth a second look in the betting for a stable which has won this in recent years.
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; dam Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 93) from a speedy family; worth a second look in the betting for a stable which has won this in recent years.

runners_data.name: Celestial Noir
runners_data.comment: One of two from her yard and of four for her owner; the betting should help guide
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 19,000gns  half-sister to winners Bellagio Man (6f AW/7f turf; RPR 91), Je Ne Sais Quoi (5f/6f including 2yo; 87) and Ridicule (Qatari 6f 2yo); one of two from her yard and of four for her owner; the betting should help guide to expectations.

runners_data.name: Lady Blanche
runners_data.comment: Represents top connections so market support would look significant.
runners_data.spotlight: January foal; £18,000 daughter of Persian Force; dam unplaced 7f/1m2f (RPR 69), half-sister to three winners, including useful  Enthrall (French 1m/1m1f); with a top yard so market support would look significant.

runners_data.name: Showmethebubbles
runners_data.comment: Yard not a regular source of first-time-out success
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; £17,000 sister to Swedish 6f winner Showcasis Oasis; dam 5f 2yo winner (RPR 81); another in the Nick Bradley silks; the percentage call is to look elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Sunrise At Dawn
runners_data.comment: Probably best to look elsewhere unless the betting strongly hints otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; dam unraced sister to US 1m Grade 3 winner Lammas; could only consider if backed.

runners_data.name: Suzie May
runners_data.comment: Stable not really known for 2yo success
runners_data.spotlight: March foal who cost 2,000gns as a yearling; half-sister to 6f winner Grey Horizon (including 2yo/AW; RPR 75); stable not really known for 2yo success.

runners_data.name: Bayside
runners_data.comment: Looks a sure-fire improver after promising debut third at Bath ten days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Made an encouraging start to her career when running on from the rear to snatch third at Bath (5f, good) ten days ago; sure to improve.

races.name: Beverley Beaker Handicap

runners_data.name: Venture Capital
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning to turf with first-time blinkers after disappointing AW runs, needs the headgear change to spark improvement
runners_data.comment: Well treated on last year's turf exploits if benefiting from first-time blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Below par in three AW outings this year but is well treated on last year's turf exploits if first-time blinkers spark him back to life.

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 198 days off but has winning 5f handicap form on good ground for current connections
runners_data.comment: Won two 5f handicaps for new yard last autumn and should be more to come this year
runners_data.spotlight: Purchased for 60,000gns from Charlie Appleby last July and looked very useful when landing 5f handicaps at Haydock (good) and Hamilton (soft) for Ed Bethell in the autumn; only had five career starts so it'll be a surprise if there isn't more to come this year; leading claims with the stable among the winners.

runners_data.name: Smart Vision
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who sets his own fractions, proven at this level with 131 days freshness potentially aiding stamina
runners_data.comment: Pair of 5f wins last autumn; fourth in this on 2025 reappearance; handy draw; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Better than ever last autumn, winning 5f handicaps at Leicester (good to soft) and Doncaster (heavy); creditable fourth (Duran second) in this race on his 2025 reappearance; likely to be competitive from a handy draw.

runners_data.name: Duran
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the same stable as Squealer, finished second in this race last year and ran well behind Smart Vision previously
runners_data.comment: Started 2025 well (including second in this on return) and claims if resuming in same form
runners_data.spotlight: Pushed the reopposing Smart Vision close at Doncaster last autumn; started last season well (including second in this race on reappearance) and should be on the premises if resuming in similar form.

runners_data.name: Squealer
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who won at York on good ground under Scott, returning off 2lb lower mark after 187 days
runners_data.comment: Below par last autumn but is on a good mark if reviving after six months off
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way last autumn but returns off 2lb lower than when winning at York (5f, good) under regular rider Rowan Scott last summer so he has plenty of handicapping scope if reviving after six months off; yard also runs Duran.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a visor, showed good York sprint form but two recent AW runs were only respectable
runners_data.comment: Not at best in two AW runs this winter but claims on last summer's York form
runners_data.spotlight: Good form in York sprints last summer; no more than respectable efforts in two AW outings this winter but feasibly treated on those York efforts if a return to turf sparks a revival.

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good current form having won twice on AW, faces step up in class back on turf
runners_data.comment: Shouldn't be too far away if he can carry good recent AW form back to the grass
runners_data.spotlight: Built on his Southwell reappearance second when seeing off five rivals back there (5f) three weeks later; respectable fifth of 12 in a competitive race at Newcastle (5f) since; while his peak RPRs have been achieved on AW he was placed at Redcar last summer and it's too soon to suggest he won't prove fully effective on the grass; could have fitness edge over some.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with first-time cheekpieces, has won twice recently on AW but returns to turf after 19 days
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins in late 2025; might have needed a recent run at Newcastle after 104 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Reacted well to a belated switch to AW at the end of 2025, winning twice over 5f at Newcastle; behind Sports Coach back there last month but it was his first outing for 104 days so he could be sharper now.

runners_data.name: I'm Next
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Tim Easterby returning after 179 days, won twice over 5f last season on similar ground
runners_data.comment: Some of 2025 reads well appeals as one who may have more to offer at some point this year
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent racer who notched two 5f wins last year, including a defeat of Sunday's Musselburgh scorer Montezuma at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) in September; not so good on final two starts but he's still relatively lightly raced as a sprinter and appeals as one who could resume his progression at some point in 2026.

runners_data.name: Acrisius
runners_data.note: Front-running type trained by the Easterby team, returning after 213 days but won over 5f at Chester on good ground
runners_data.comment: 5f Chester win last year; also went close on 2025 reappearance so could be ready to roll
runners_data.spotlight: Successful over 5f at Chester (5f, good) last July; also went close on his 2025 reappearance which provides hope that he may be ready to roll after seven months off; drawn widest.

races.paceDynamic: Smart Vision will lead from the gates with minimal pressure, setting a moderate tempo over this sharp 5f track. Venture Capital, Sports Coach, I'm Next and Acrisius can press on but are unlikely to challenge for the lead early. The lack of genuine pace-setters means Smart Vision can dictate terms unchallenged, creating a scenario where the pace builds gradually rather than being fierce throughout. This controlled tempo strongly favors hold-up horses who can finish fast over prominent racers who may get caught out by the kick when it comes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision leads unchallenged and sets moderate fractions
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace allows hold-up horses to position perfectly and unleash their finishing kicks. Corolla Point and Duran can time their runs to perfection while prominent racers find themselves outpaced by the change of gear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision maintains stamina and the chasing pack fails to organize
scenarios.body: The front-runner uses his tactical advantage to repel late challengers who leave their runs too late. His proven 5f winning form at this level becomes decisive when others struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Prosper
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and prominent horses can stalk comfortably
scenarios.body: Venture Capital and Sports Coach can sit in perfect striking positions without being asked early questions. Their superior class tells when they have energy reserves for the crucial final furlong surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Longshot
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems or interference disrupts the finish
scenarios.body: The tight finish sees several horses hampered or forced wide, allowing a well-positioned outsider to sneak through. Tiriac or I'm Next benefit from cleaner passages while fancied runners hit trouble.

watchPoints.text: Smart Vision could steal this if allowed uncontested lead as no other genuine front-runners will challenge his pace-setting role
Venture Capital needs first-time blinkers to work immediately as his recent AW form suggests he's lost his way without headgear help
Corolla Point makes debut for new connections after 198 days but his winning 5f handicap form for Bethell suggests he's well-treated
Both Duran and Squealer trained by Nigel Tinkler are returning from winter breaks and stable is 0 from 18 in last 14 days
Air Force One sports a visor and needs to prove his York sprint form translates after modest recent AW efforts

races.name: 140th Year Of The Watt Memorial Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Elysian Flame
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 209 days off but has proven stamina for this extended trip and good record on similar going.
runners_data.comment: Smart in 2024 but last autumn's well-held fourth at Ayr was first run since
runners_data.spotlight: Developed into a pretty smart staying handicapper on the Flat for Mick and David Easterby in 2021, finishing third in 2m4f handicaps at Royal Ascot and Glorious Goodwood; respectable fifth of 32 in the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f) in October of that year but not seen again until fourth of six at Ayr (1m5f, good to soft) last September; there was enough in that to suggest he retains ability but he's been absent for another seven months and isn't the easiest to assess.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Natural leader with course and distance form but heavy defeat on AW last time raises questions about current form.
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; latest heavy AW defeat came in strong race; this turf race is easier; player
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent racer who posted four wins in the second half of last year, including a C&D defeat of Charging Thunder on good; suffered a heavy defeat on AW last time but it was in a strong Good Friday race at Newcastle and Charging Thunder was once again behind him; a bold show seems likely in these much calmer waters back on turf.

runners_data.name: Anniversary
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with scope for improvement at just 4 years old and shaped well when second at Southwell recently.
runners_data.comment: Races freely but still relatively unexposed and latest Kempton fifth came in a good race
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has had only seven races; can race freely but there's still a feeling he could have a bigger performance in him and he shaped quite well under a change of tactics (went from the front) when 4l fifth of nine in the Queen's Prize at Kempton (2m, AW) 18 days ago.

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying bottom weight with new headgear and trainer, but form suggests he's past his peak at 8 years old.
runners_data.comment: Last of six in 2m AW handicap back on Flat last month and others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful in this sphere at his peak but it's doubtful he still retains that level of ability, finishing last of six in 2m AW handicap at Southwell back on the Flat last month.

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 5lb apprentice jockey but poor recent form and already beaten by Sax Appeal at this course and distance.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal will lead from the outset with no other confirmed front runners in this field, creating a sustainable tempo over the 2m trip on good ground at Beverley. The prominent runner Elysian Flame may track the leader early, but the three hold-up horses Anniversary, Wahraan, and Charging Thunder will settle further back, banking on the extended distance suiting their patient tactics. With only one natural leader against multiple closers, this sets up a tactical battle where the pace is unlikely to be testing early. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up runners who can exploit what should be a modest gallop and time their challenges late in a small field where positioning won't be crucial.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal sets only a steady tempo as expected with no pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: The patient trio get perfect conditions to unleash their finishing kicks, with Anniversary and Charging Thunder able to use their class advantage. The soft pace allows them to overcome their tactical disadvantage of racing from behind in a small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal gets away with very soft fractions and the hold-up horses leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage while the closers struggle to make up ground in time over the extended trip. Sax Appeal's recent course and distance victory over Charging Thunder becomes highly relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactics Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Elysian Flame tracks Sax Appeal closely and applies pressure from halfway
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old's stamina reserves kick in as the pace lifts, allowing her to grind down the leader while staying ahead of the late closers. Her proven ability at extended distances on good ground becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Wahraan
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and turns into a sprint finish where his lower weight becomes crucial
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old's 12lb weight advantage allows him to quicken better than his higher-rated rivals in a slowly-run race. His trainer change and headgear addition suggest connections expect improvement from his last disappointing effort.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Sax Appeal gets away with pedestrian fractions early as the hold-up horses may leave themselves too much to do
Monitor Anniversary's position turning for home as his hold-up style could be problematic in this small field
Observe Wahraan's early settling pattern as his headgear change might affect his usual patient tactics
Watch Charging Thunder's jockey Mason Paetel claiming 5lbs as inexperience could cost vital lengths at crucial moments
Check Elysian Flame's jumping off given her long absence and whether she tracks the leaders closely enough

races.name: Diony Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Stay Salty

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos

runners_data.spotlight: Won 7f Lingfield (AW) maiden on his third start for Dylan Cunha but hasn't reproduced that in two subsequent AW handicaps; needs to resume his progress back on turf.

runners_data.name: Top Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 144-day layoff, perfectly positioned if pace is strong as expected
runners_data.comment: Well held on AW last November but showed promise on turf before that; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well held on AW in November but did show some promise at up to on turf prior to that; off for five months ahead of this handicap debut, with the betting perhaps the best guide to expectations.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Prominent racer off 264-day break, progressive profile last season but long absence is concerning
runners_data.comment: Off since July but progressed with each start last year; check betting on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Advanced her RPR with each start last summer, finishing second of 16 in a restricted novice at York (7f, good) in July; while that York form hasn't really worked out, she still brings unexposed potential to this handicap debut after nearly nine months off; check the betting.

runners_data.name: Reliable Ricki
runners_data.note: Non-runner, front-runner who would have added to early pace pressure
runners_data.comment: AW maiden win in autumn; mark of 75 demands more but probably more to come; drawn widest
runners_data.spotlight: Third on first two starts before improving to make it third time lucky in maidens at Wolverhampton (7f) in September; while his opening handicap mark isn't obviously generous his useful pedigree provides the hope for further progress; outside stall could be tricky.

runners_data.name: Ubetterseethis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 12 juvenile starts, likely to track the pace but may lack finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Had 12 starts at 2 so he's much more exposed than most; gelded ahead more return
runners_data.spotlight: Kept busy as a 2yo with 12 runs, winning a 7f Chester seller (good to firm); left the impression a stiff 1m at Pontefract (soft) just stretched him on final start; this slightly shorter trip could therefore suit on reappearance but he has a much more exposed profile than most; has been gelded.

runners_data.name: Solar Cooper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching trainers after disappointing 2024, well-handicapped if retaining ability
runners_data.comment: Failed to progress last year, including sixth when favourite for handicap debut; new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress from his opening third in three subsequent starts for Brian Ellison last year, despite being 7-4 favourite for handicap debut at Thirsk (6f, good) in August when last seen; returns from nearly nine months off, under the care of a new trainer.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 211 days, will ensure strong early pace but stamina questions remain
runners_data.comment: Promise on second of three AW starts last year; off 211 days ahead of this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Left debut behind when promising third of 13 at Newcastle (6f) last August; went off favourite for a Wolverhampton novice (6f again) the following month but stopped quickly and finished sixth; absent for seven months ahead of this handicap and turf debut.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: Course winner who beat Lyrical Song last time, prominent style but poorly placed tactically here
runners_data.comment: Saw off Lyrical Song to win in October but well held final two runs; Tudhope on stablemate
runners_data.spotlight: Second success when making all from Lyrical Song in 7f Musselburgh handicap (soft) last October but well beaten in both subsequent starts and Danny Tudhope, who was on board at Musselburgh, partners stablemate Sandy Craic.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer resuming after 197 days, showed promise at Carlisle and suits expected pace setup
runners_data.comment: Promise in three runs last year; potential improver in handicaps after gelding operation
runners_data.spotlight: Three outings over 6f last year, showing promise when keeping on for close fourth at Carlisle (good) on second start; blew the start at Ayr (soft) four weeks later, so can have that fourth of eight marked up slightly; subsequently gelded; potential improver and one of the more likely types, particularly if backed.

runners_data.name: Lady Hornblower
runners_data.note: Course winner with prominent style, returning after 193 days but has proven 7f+ stamina
runners_data.comment: First then second in maiden/novice over C&D last year; respected handicap newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: Won a fast-ground C&D novice last August and bumped into subsequent Listed runner-up Caim when second under a penalty back here (soft) in September; never involved in a big-field sales race at Newmarket final start but those C&D performances provide hope that she could go well now handicapping after a six-month break.

runners_data.name: Space Moon
runners_data.note: Recent run suggests return to form, prominent style with just 2-day turnaround raising stamina concerns

races.paceDynamic: Stay Salty, Reliable Ricki (now non-runner), and Indefensible will ensure a strong gallop from the outset over this extended 7½f trip. With Stay Salty likely to take them along from the front, supported by the prominent racers Lyrical Song, King Of Chaos, and Lady Hornblower tracking close behind, this becomes a stamina test. The sustained pace will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses Top Lad, Solar Cooper, and Cosmic Man to deliver their finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours closers and hold-up performers who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalize Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners maintain a strong gallop through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The pace will tell in the final 2f, allowing hold-up horses to sweep past tiring leaders with their superior finishing kicks. Top Lad and Solar Cooper are perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can secure an ideal tracking position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: They can strike at the optimal moment before the closers arrive, having saved enough energy while staying close to the pace. King Of Chaos and Lady Hornblower have the tactical speed to execute this perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Stay Salty can dictate more moderate fractions than expected
scenarios.body: The leader can maintain enough in reserve to repel late challenges, particularly with his proven stamina over 7f+ trips. Stay Salty's front-running style becomes an asset rather than a liability in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast with multiple horses vying for the lead
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse with a turn of foot can win regardless of early positioning. This chaos scenario opens the door for any runner with residual ability.

watchPoints.text: Stay Salty and Indefensible setting unsustainable fractions in the opening 3f could set up a pace collapse
Top Lad and Solar Cooper both returning from 140+ day breaks, watch for fitness on seasonal debuts
King Of Chaos tracking the early pace smoothly, as his strike rate improves significantly when positioned prominently
Space Moon running on just 2-day turnaround, monitor for any signs of previous race taking its toll
Lady Hornblower's early positioning behind the front rank, as her course-winning form gives her a tactical edge here

races.name: Spillers Powering Your Winners Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Holly Mist
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with consistent place record who should improve returned to turf from recent all-weather third
runners_data.comment: Good handicap debut when third (1m, AW) ten days ago; unexposed and might be the answer
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in all four starts, including when keeping-on third on her handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) ten days ago; same mark and should be fine returned to turf; fitness is guaranteed and she's a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Blufferonthebus
runners_data.note: Course winner returning from 120-day break with solid hold-up style but fitness concerns after long layoff
runners_data.comment: Won two 7f handicaps in November; stays this trip and she's not readily dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner (7.5f, soft) in 2024 who won two 7f handicaps (soft/AW) last November; blew the start when beating one home (same mark) the following month and absent since; stays this trip, though, and she's not readily dismissed.

runners_data.name: Fire Eyes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three recent wins but notably racing without usual tongue-tie and cheekpieces today
runners_data.comment: All three 2025 wins featured headgear; no aids again, but fit and on last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won three turf handicaps (1m/7f) in 2025, all in a tongue-tie and the latest with cheekpieces on for the first time; no headgear for either start last month (probably didn't stay 1m2f last time) and the accessories are missing again; back on her last winning mark, though.

runners_data.name: Wondrous Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 166-day absence with solid course record but major fitness question
runners_data.comment: 11.5f winner on handicap debut in June; back on that winning mark for this return
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Lingfield (11.5f, good to soft) on her handicap debut in June and well backed when a fair fifth of 14 over this sort of trip at Newmarket (good) in October; would likely appreciate any rain and she's back on her winning mark for this reappearance.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and dual course winner wearing cheekpieces, just eight days since last run
runners_data.comment: Dual 1m2f course winner who ran well at 1m when last tried nearly 2 years ago; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Dual winner here (1m2f) including when she beat Dandy's Angel on good ground last May; 0-7 subsequently but she went close at Redcar in August and last week's pipe-opener at Pontefract (raced freely) should help; first go at this sort of trip since second of six at Doncaster in June 2024 and she could go well.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Prominent style suited to this trip extension, 12-race maiden but showed good form in October
runners_data.comment: Second twice over this sort of trip in October; latest start (1m2f) can be excused; chance
runners_data.spotlight: 12-race maiden but she was in good form when runner-up twice over this sort of trip in October, notably when beaten a neck at Nottingham (good); step up to 1m2f backfired when favourite at Chelmsford (AW) the following month but she's back down in distance for this return; respected.

runners_data.name: Catton Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won at Carlisle over Blufferonthebus but returning from 212-day layoff
runners_data.comment: Dual Carlisle winner who ran well at Thirsk in September when last seen; market may help
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well to beat Blufferonthebus at Carlisle (her only other win also came there) in June; good effort when second of 11 at Thirsk (also 1m, soft) in September when last seen; also ran well on her return in 2024 but could beat only Dandy's Angel when making her comeback in this race last year; any rain would help and market may guide on this reappearance.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist and six-time course winner but 0-10 since last victory and long absence
runners_data.comment: Six-time course winner (1m2f); goes on any ground; nothing wrong with this mark if ready
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time course winner (all 1m2f) who goes on any ground and finished second in this on her first start of 2023; 0-10 since her last win in July, however, and she was 50-1 when suffering big defeat on her reappearance in this race last year; nothing wrong with this mark if she is ready to roll.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who won over course and distance in June but showed stamina doubts in last two starts
runners_data.comment: Three good 1m2f runs in 2025 included win here; back in trip for return but not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Justified short odds in 1m2f handicap here (good to firm) in June and ran well when second in similar race here next time; didn't see out final two starts last year, so maybe this drop back in trip can assist on her reappearance.

runners_data.name: Special Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tendency to fade in finish, returning from 204-day break with fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Appeared to improve on last qualifying run and she's unexposed on this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Appeared to show improved form when fourth of five at Southwell (1m, AW) in September on her final qualifying run; assessor probably hasn't left much to chance but she's the least exposed of these and may be able to have a say on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Quirke On Parole is the sole confirmed front-runner and will get an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable pace without pressure from other speed horses. Princess Niyla and Glorious Kitty will track prominently but neither has early pace to challenge for the lead, leaving Quirke On Parole to dictate terms. The hold-up brigade including Holly Mist, Fire Eyes, Wondrous Light and Catton Lady will settle at the back and rely on a finishing kick. This honest pace scenario clearly favours the prominent and hold-up horses who can time their runs, as they won't face a truly searching gallop early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Quirke On Parole maintains stamina over this extended trip
scenarios.body: The front-runner gets easy fractions and kicks clear in the straight while the hold-up horses find the pace too honest to close effectively. Quirke On Parole's June course win over this trip proves the stamina is there.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and develops into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to get into perfect striking positions and unleash superior finishing kicks. Holly Mist's consistent place record and Fire Eyes' recent wins make them perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Niyla or Glorious Kitty improve their positions early
scenarios.body: The prominent pair get first run on the leader and benefit from racing closer to a steady pace without using excessive energy. Princess Niyla's dual course wins over similar trips give her a clear edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Quirke On Parole goes too slow and gets swamped late
scenarios.body: The entire field bunches up turning for home and it becomes a pure sprint finish where ratings matter most. Fire Eyes and Holly Mist have shown the best recent form to capitalize on such circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Special Breeze has a known tendency to fade in the finish and faces a significant fitness test after 204 days off
Quirke On Parole showed stamina limitations in his last two starts over similar trips which could be crucial as the lone leader
Three key contenders return from breaks exceeding 160 days with Wondrous Light, Catton Lady and Dandy's Angel all facing fitness questions
Fire Eyes races without his usual tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time since winning three races earlier this year
Princess Niyla drops back to a trip where she's won twice at this course and races just eight days after her last run

races.name: Racing Again Next Thursday Handicap

runners_data.name: Freddy Robinson
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent Beverley record who benefits from lack of early pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Won here (1m2f) in 2024; has run well at this track on other occasions and stays this trip
runners_data.spotlight: 1-23 on the Flat but the win came at this track (1m2f, good to soft) in June 2024; plenty of other good efforts here, including over this trip, and he was a winner over hurdles in December; should benefit from his reappearance in early March; can go well.

runners_data.name: Arth's Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse threatening to break maiden but may struggle to get competitive position from rear
runners_data.comment: Only just picked off over 1m4f on AW ten days ago; player if transferring that to turf
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 but he's threatening to win a race and was only just picked off when tackling 1m4f for the first time at Southwell (AW) ten days ago; slight question to answer on just this second turf start but otherwise a player from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Sea Master
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner returning from 181-day break, likely to get uncontested lead

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying first-time cheekpieces for new connections after 75-day break
runners_data.comment: Won January AW h'cap (1m4f) in cheekpieces; those aids are missing for this stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed 8yo but he won for the sixth time when landing 1m4f handicap at Kempton (AW; first-time cheekpieces) on his penultimate start for Shaun Harris; 4lb higher for this stable debut (same owner) and the cheekpieces are missing again.

runners_data.name: Irv
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up runner with course form but 4lb higher than last win and 89 days since last run
runners_data.comment: 50-1 when beaten 10l on his return in Wolverhampton classified (1m4f, AW) in January
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner in 2022 who last won at Pontefract (also 1m2f, good to firm) in June 2024; 50-1 when beaten 10l on his comeback in a Wolverhampton classified (1m4f, AW) in January; others look safer.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course and distance success but 231 days since last outing
runners_data.comment: Two summer wins came wearing cheekpeices (1m4f and here over 1m2f); no headgear this time
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back wins last summer came over 1m2f here (soft) and when narrowly making all at Catterick (1m4f, good); both wins came under Tom Kiely-Marshall but they also featured cheekpieces, which are missing for this comeback; mark is fine if he is ready.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare struggling for form and needing significant improvement at the weights

runners_data.name: Sugarpiehoneybunch
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with stamina credentials but returning from 169-day absence

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse seeking first career win but showed promise when third at Catterick seven days ago
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in 19 attempts but not disgraced on last three starts; might be on the premises
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to score in 19 attempts but not disgraced on last three starts, beaten just over 2l at Catterick (1m4f, good) under Warren Fentiman one week ago; stiff 1m4f is not certain to suit but he might be on the premises.

runners_data.name: Nymphaea
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse winless in nine starts but has shown some promise over middle distances
runners_data.comment: Disappointed latest (AW) but she's not ruled out in her first handicap on turf
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 but she wasn't far away at Newcastle (1m4f) in February and went pretty close at Southwell (1m6f) the following month; disappointed in Lingfield classified (also AW) three weeks ago but she's not entirely ruled out in this first turf handicap.

runners_data.name: Havachoc
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent back-to-back wins on all-weather switching back to turf

runners_data.name: Highfield Comrade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form including classified win at Southwell
runners_data.comment: Third on turf in August and improved on AW this year; won't lack for fitness; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 41333 since switched to AW, the win in a Southwell classified over 1m3f in January; respectable third on turf at Thirsk (1m4f, good to firm) in August, however, and he won't lack for fitness back on grass.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Master is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the gates, likely getting an uncontested lead with the field heavily skewed towards hold-up runners. With 10 of 12 horses preferring to come from behind, Freddy Robinson and Inspiring Speeches offer the only prominent challenge to Sea Master's early control. This setup creates a moderate pace through the middle furlongs before a cavalry charge of hold-up horses attempts to reel in the leaders. The lack of early pace pressure strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions without expending energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Master gets an easy lead and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows the leader to save energy for a strong finish while the mass of hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from poor positions. Sea Master's stamina-laden pedigree and previous course success become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If Freddy Robinson or Inspiring Speeches can track Sea Master without over-racing
scenarios.body: The prominent runners benefit from ideal positioning behind the uncontested leader, allowing them to strike at the optimal moment while hold-up horses are still organizing their challenges. Course experience and tactical positioning prove crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens unexpectedly or Sea Master stops in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A faster early gallop or leader faltering allows the better hold-up horses to unleash their finishing kicks from their preferred positions. The class and recent form of horses like Arth's Gold and Havachoc come to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a true staying test or pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: Extreme tactical circumstances favor an overlooked runner who gets the perfect trip through the field. The race becomes about stamina and finishing kick rather than class or recent form.

watchPoints.text: Sea Master must be watched for fitness after 181-day layoff as the race outcome heavily depends on his stamina lasting
Freddy Robinson's ability to settle prominently without over-racing will determine if he can capitalize on ideal pace setup
Arth's Gold needs to be positioned closer than usual to have any chance given the lack of early pace
The inside draw positions of several hold-up horses could create traffic problems in a slowly-run race
Any early pressure on Sea Master from Inspiring Speeches or Freddy Robinson would completely change the race dynamic
